verdict_summary.headline: The five reported violations contain no real pin drift and no real vendor material; the two substantive items are an auditor classification error on historical evidence and a filename-based vendor false positive. The separately meaningful item is an unverified implementation (terrain / initialized-state interfaces), which the auditor does not check at all.

lifecycle_audit.limitation: Independent Linux reconstruction and reset only; no flight or MATLAB numeric oracle

findings.statement: The model.cpp size/hash drift reported by the audit is a classification error: the historical evidence chain legitimately pins a superseded 1864 B wrapper whose bytes are preserved in-repo. The auditor must bind a declared historical identity to its archived copy instead of to today's canonical file.

The vendor-artifact check fires on 33 tracked WSL host-probe receipts purely because their filenames embed the probed distro name. None contains vendor bytes and all report an empty found list; the rule must classify by extension and content, not by path text.

The two interfaces added to the current wrapper after the historical build (same-source terrain input, initialized-state semantics) are implemented and tracked but were never driven by any probe and have no assertions. They are an unverified implementation surface, and the audit does not check this at all.
Three violations are Windows-vs-WSL path-boundary artefacts. The Linux-resident /root build and cold-rebuild libraries cannot be resolved on this host; the evidence never claimed they could be.

The pinned historical digest is not a git object on the wrapper path and never was committed there, because the build consumed an uncommitted 1864 B working-tree variant. Re-verifiability now depends on a single tracked frozen snapshot; the correction must fail closed if that archive is absent.
